# LED watch pin map (generated by tools/generate.py - do not edit)

MCU: ATtiny3217, VQFN-24. Board rev A.

| Signal | MCU pin | Port | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW_A | 19 | PC2 | button A (2 o'clock), to GND via 1k, 100 nF at MCU; fully async pin |
| SW_B | 20 | PC3 | button B (4 o'clock), to GND via 1k, 100 nF at MCU; NOT async: wake with BOTHEDGES/LEVEL |
| ACC_INT | 17 | PC0 | LIS2DH12 INT1, push-pull from the sensor; NOT async: BOTHEDGES/LEVEL |
| SDA | 15 | PB1 | TWI0, 4.7k pull-up (fitted with U2) |
| SCL | 16 | PB0 | TWI0, 4.7k pull-up (fitted with U2) |
| XT1 | 13 | PB3 | TOSC1, 32.768 kHz 7 pF crystal |
| XT2 | 14 | PB2 | TOSC2 |
| UPDI | 23 | PA0 | pogo pad TP1 |
| TX | 24 | PA1 | USART0 TxD (alternate pin), pad TP3 |
| RTC | 1 | PA2 | EVOUT0 test pad TP4 (route RTC/PIT event here to measure the crystal) |
| L0 | 2 | PA3 | charlieplex line, 100 R series |
| L1 | 5 | PA4 | charlieplex line, 100 R series |
| L2 | 6 | PA5 | charlieplex line, 100 R series |
| L3 | 7 | PA6 | charlieplex line, 100 R series |
| L4 | 8 | PA7 | charlieplex line, 100 R series |
| L5 | 9 | PB7 | charlieplex line, 100 R series |
| L6 | 10 | PB6 | charlieplex line, 100 R series |
| L7 | 11 | PB5 | charlieplex line, 100 R series |
| L8 | 12 | PB4 | charlieplex line, 100 R series |

Spare, not connected: PC1 (pin 18), PC4 (pin 21), PC5 (pin 22).
LIS2DH12: I2C address 0x19 (SA0 tied high), CS high, on the TOP side (+Z out of the dial).

Index = firmware numbering: 0-59 minutes clockwise from 12, 60-71 hours from 12.
Light LED i: line A high, line K low, all other lines input with INPUT_DISABLE.

## Firmware rules from the hardware review (007)

- Never drive VDD from the programmer: there is no VDD pad; program from the cell (UPDI + GND).
- BOD off in sleep (or sampled at 125 Hz): continuous BOD costs ~20 uA.
- In sleep set INPUT_DISABLE (or drive low) on all 9 LED lines and on the spare pins.
- When switching LEDs, set all line DIR bits to input first, then set the new pair.
- Refuse to light LEDs below ~2.4 V (measure VDD against the internal reference).
